name: NY-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: Open seat after Espaillat lost renomination, but Democratic nominee Avila Chevalier won a contested primary with strong fundraising
Republican Jomo Williams has no reported fundraising or outside support
Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 97%
model.rationale: The district's D+32 baseline makes a Republican win implausible even with the incumbent off the ballot. Avila Chevalier raised over $1.3 million and drew heavy outside spending in the primary, while Williams shows no measurable campaign infrastructure, so the forecast sits slightly above the baseline margin.
model.watch: A scandal or primary-faction backlash against the Democratic nominee could narrow the margin, though a Republican win would still require an unprecedented collapse.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Adriano Espaillat (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
This northern Manhattan and Bronx seat is one of the most Democratic-leaning districts in the country, with a partisan lean of D+32. Adriano Espaillat is not on the ballot after losing renomination, but the Democratic nominee, Darializa Avila Chevalier, enters the general election with a strong campaign: she raised about $1.35 million and attracted nearly $1.9 million in outside support during a contested primary. Republican Jomo Williams reports no fundraising, cash on hand, or outside spending.

Prediction markets price the Democratic side at roughly 97%, and no expert raters list the race as competitive. The forecast expects a comfortable Democratic hold, with the margin near the district's fundamentals and modest uncertainty given the open seat and absence of general-election polling.
